scenes.voiceover: Is America really pushing out its best Indian engineers? Four countries say: send them our way.
scenes.image_prompt: Airport departures board showing London, Toronto, Berlin, Sydney with Indian tech professional silhouette

scenes.voiceover: Sixty-five percent of US employers have lost foreign talent this year. EB-2 India is completely shut until September.
scenes.image_prompt: Large 65% stat with cracked American flag and fading H-1B visa stamp

scenes.voiceover: Britain's Global Talent visa needs no job offer, no sponsor. Processing? Three weeks. Not three decades.
scenes.image_prompt: London skyline with Union Jack and UK Global Talent Visa stats

scenes.voiceover: Canada processed over one hundred ten thousand Express Entry invitations last year, targeting tech workers specifically.
scenes.image_prompt: Toronto CN Tower skyline with Express Entry 110,000+ invitations stat

scenes.voiceover: Germany offers permanent residency in twenty-one months. The EB-2 India wait? Eighty-plus years. Do the math.
scenes.image_prompt: Split screen Germany 21 months PR versus US 80+ year EB-2 wait comparison

scenes.voiceover: Indians hold seventy percent of all H-1B approvals. Amazon alone sponsors nearly five thousand. This is America's engineering backbone.
scenes.image_prompt: H-1B statistics dashboard with 70% hero stat and employer bar chart

scenes.voiceover: The question isn't whether Indian engineers will leave America. It's which country gets them first.
scenes.image_prompt: World map with glowing arrows from US to UK, Canada, Germany, Australia
